output.brief: The 2026 Pellacott VA-220 valves are defective, and the leak-test paperwork behind their good score does not reflect real testing. The rig that was meant to test them was out of service from 9 Jan 2026. Its last test cycle was 18 Dec 2025. No other rig has a VA-220 program loaded. 31 of 36 certificates reuse four copied sequences of values. Your lab's helium retest of never-installed valves found 11% of Pellacott 2026 valves leaking at the seat, against 1% for 2025 builds and 0% for Durrant-Hale. Teardown shows a deformed, unseated seal. Claim rates are the same across new and legacy installers and across firmware 4.1 and 4.2. Installers and firmware are therefore not the cause. Whether the new Corlin seal or the new Line 3 assembly is responsible cannot yet be separated, so do not order a return to the old seal yet. Do not release the six held lots on fresh certificates, and do not penalise installers. Quarantine 2026-built Pellacott stock, suspend dock-to-stock, and release only after Brenmoor's own helium testing. Plan for the line stoppage, for example by raising Durrant-Hale volume. Then re-audit Pellacott's records and check other suppliers' certificates, since the 96 average conformance score is unverified. Confidence is high on the main conclusions and lower on the seal-versus-line question and on other suppliers.
